_metadata.purpose: x08: a bounded batch of owner proposals (2026-10-19), processed locally with deterministic checks and a main-session critique; no model or review calls, no bank additions

provenance.clarification: Deb West, Sentinel_d1ed861b870c81919a92a44d2b44aa39: 'I like Cairo better. Bill is for Gates and Nye. What else would you do for Bread + Fool ? Let me know. Yes like swinging a broom. If you have something better I'm all ears'
provenance.sweepAndBeggar: Deb West, Sentinel_c7e7ceee8c4881918fcd4d014680635e: 'Sweep is perfect. I still think beggar is best. Even though all beggars aren't fools, it's a common trope. The foolish beggar'
provenance.parentDisagreement: parent, Sentinel_cb0a68f5986c819189ae7fd18fa5a1e6: the FOOL side of BEGGAR is not supported enough; keep the pair open
provenance.finalBeggar: Deb West, Sentinel_c82fadae8c488191978b659fb20eee30: 'Just go with the medieval assocation. In medieval times a fool may be begging for bread on the street, no?'

_metadata.workflow: An owner proposal is the source. 'coordinator-accepted' = the parent approved it after local checks (overrides.json coordinator_accept, not an owner decision). 'owner-selected' = the owner chose it explicitly (human_approved, by owner).
_metadata.checks: bank membership and spelling, stored hints and preferences for the pair, rejections.json, the hint rule (hintProblem), served uses of the same hint, facts in the explanation

items.why: A flea circus is a famous old sideshow, and circus acrobats climb ladders up to the trapeze.
items.critique: Fair. The LADDER side is a circus scene rather than a set phrase.

items.why: Solo means alone, like solitary, and a pilot's first flight alone is their solo (Han Solo is a famous pilot, too).
items.critique: Strong on PILOT (a pilot's first solo flight, plus Han Solo). SOLO is close to a synonym of SOLITARY, which makes that side easy rather than clever.

items.why: Aflac, the insurance business, is famous for its quacking duck mascot.
items.critique: A broad US brand reference. The BUSINESS side is generic (any company is a business), and it is US-centric.

items.why: A parrot is a bird, and the classic pirate keeps one on his shoulder.

items.outcome: kept as the owner's original proposal: held, not selected
items.detail: Proposed as ARCHEOLOGY + CAPITAL; the bank spells the word ARCHAEOLOGY, so the pair was matched to that bank word (nothing added to the bank). Egypt is a country, not a capital; the owner chose CAIRO instead.

items.why: Cairo is the capital of Egypt, and it sits beside the Giza pyramids, a center of archaeology.
A doodle is a quick drawing, and doodles are poodle-mix dogs like the goldendoodle.
items.critique: Good double meaning. DOODLE is close to a synonym of DRAWING, so that side is easy.

items.why: Bill Nye is the Science Guy, and Bill Gates's last name is GATE with an S.
items.critique: An honest name bridge: Gates, not gate, which the explanation says.

items.why: Picture a foolish storybook character begging for a crust of bread.
history: owner preferred BEGGAR: 'the foolish beggar' trope (Sentinel_c7e7ceee...)
parent disagreed: FOOL side not supported enough; pair kept open (Sentinel_cb0a68f5...)
final owner choice: 'Just go with the medieval assocation' (Sentinel_c82fadae...)
items.detail: A loose invented scene. Not a proven medieval trope, a historical fact about fools, or a claim that beggars are fools.

items.outcome: parent alternatives, not selected, not stored
items.detail: SUCKER was a weak parent brainstorm. MONEY: bread is slang for money, and 'a fool and his money are soon parted'.

items.outcome: kept as the owner's earlier proposal: held, not selected
items.detail: Route confirmed by the owner ('like swinging a broom'); she then chose SWEEP.

items.why: A sweep is a broad, swinging motion, and sweeping is how you clean the floor.
Firefighters put out fires with water, and a bucket is for carrying water.
items.critique: Direct but plain; WATER is a common hint word (four other served pairs).

items.why: Banjos ring out at a barn dance, and a banjo picks out the notes of a tune.
items.critique: The BARN side is a scene (barn dance). The NOTE side is generic: any instrument plays notes.
